subjects.name: Massachusetts Peace Officer Standards and Training Commission

summary: A Sixteenth Minute episode in which Jamie Loftus tries to identify the unnamed Boston police officer who went viral in 2023 for crashing down a City Hall Plaza slide, and finds how Massachusetts police shield officer records from the public.

evidence.note: Loftus introduces her own show Sixteenth Minute; episode republished in the BtB feed
Video of the officer's slide crash posted on Twitter in early August 2023
FOIA incident report dates the crash to late July 2023 during a festival
Conger explains the Massachusetts privacy exemption used to withhold the name
Police disciplinary database from the 2020 post-Floyd oversight commission released
Raymond describes the POST Commission and his records requests to every department
Appellate document cites fear of officers being mocked on social media
Spring 2024 state high court transparency ruling discussed
Search through precinct officers turns up misconduct records of other cops

notes: Crossover from Jamie Loftus's Sixteenth Minute. The officer was never identified, so the primary subject is the incident rather than a person and roles are left empty. Covered span starts with the 2020 founding of the POST Commission, which gets a long interview segment. No theme for public records or government transparency; policing-incarceration covers it.
